Luxembourg Airport Halts Flights Over Unauthorized Drones — Luxembourg’s sole international airport temporarily suspended flight operations on Sept. 18 after unauthorized drones were detected operating near and over the airfield. Flight restrictions were imposed to protect passengers, flight crews, and aircraft, with normal operations resuming on Saturday alongside lingering schedule disruptions.

US Law Makes Deporting Ukrainian Children Grounds for Sanctions — US President Donald Trump has signed into law H.R. 5334, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which formally establishes the forcible transfer and deportation of Ukrainian children as grounds for US sanctions, Bring Kids Back UA announced. The statute imposes asset freezes and travel bans on individuals, guardianship bodies, and transport operators involved directly or indirectly in child removals.

Poland Joins European Coalition on Ballistic Missile Defense — Poland has joined a European defense coalition dedicated to developing joint counter-ballistic missile capabilities alongside Ukraine and nine other European states, President Volodymyr Zelensky and Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced on Friday. Tusk described Poland’s omission from the initiative’s initial July launch in Paris as a misunderstanding, noting that Polish defense contractors are reviewing options to contribute i

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Command Posts and Training Ground — Ukrainian Defense Forces have struck Russian UAV command posts, the “Vostochny” military training ground, a logistics warehouse, and an ammunition depot across occupied Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia regions. Strikes hit drone command centers in Luhanske, Pokrovsk, and five settlements across Zaporizhzhia, alongside confirmed damage to an 80P6 radar in Russia’s Smolensk region.

AfD Leaders Plan Talks With Putin Envoy on Russian Gas — Leaders of Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party are preparing to meet with Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev next year to discuss resuming Russian natural gas supplies to Germany, Reuters reported. The prospective talks between AfD co-chairs Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla and Dmitriev sparked condemnation from German lawmakers in the CDU and Greens, who denounced the initiative as political betrayal and a threa

Ukraine Backs Foreign Recruitment Center for National Guard — The Ukrainian government has approved the creation of a specialized Recruitment Center for Foreigners and Stateless Persons within the National Guard, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said. The center will oversee the entire intake pipeline – from screening and interviews to training – aiming to expedite the deployment of foreign contract volunteers to combat units.

Germany Must Prepare Entire Society for War, Military Chief Warns — Germany must mobilize its entire society, industry, and armed forces to prepare for national defense and the risk of war, Inspector General of the Bundeswehr Carsten Breuer warned at the IISS Prague Defense Summit. Breuer emphasized that military and technological strength alone cannot counter evolving security challenges, urging Germany to absorb lessons from Russia’s invasion of Ukraine ahead of a 2029 target for full Bundeswe

UK Military Sites Targeted by Drones Over 300 Times in Year — British defense sites recorded 340 security incidents involving drones in the 12 months to August 2026, marking a significant increase from 250 in 2025 and 126 in 2024, according to figures reported by The Independent. UK Armed Forces Minister Louise Sandher-Jones said the government takes the threat seriously, explaining the increase partly reflects improved monitoring after 44 strategic military sites were designated restricted airs

US, Denmark, and Greenland Agree on Expanded Military Presence — The US, Denmark, and Greenland have reached a defense agreement allowing Washington to expand its military footprint across Greenland while barring non-NATO adversaries from establishing bases or making sensitive investments, US President Donald Trump announced on Friday, Sept. 18. The accord grants the US permanent overflight, transit, and basing rights that would endure even if Greenland achieves independence.

Putin Claims Readiness to Restore Relations With Europe — Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed that Moscow is ready to restore relations and cooperate with its European neighbors, asserting that Russia has no hostile intentions toward Europe. Putin accused European leaders of discussing war preparations to distract from domestic economic problems, while alleging NATO continues destabilizing expansions.

Trump’s UNGA Schedule Omits Bilateral Meeting With Zelensky — President Volodymyr Zelensky is not included among the leaders scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with US President Donald Trump at the UN General Assembly in New York. Two senior Ukrainian officials confirmed that no meeting is currently finalized. Trump’s announced itinerary includes addresses to the UNGA and bilateral meetings with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, GCC leaders, and acting Ven

Russian Strike on Kharkiv Region Kills 4 — A Russian drone strike on a private residential house in Balakliya, Kharkiv region, killed four people late Friday, Sept. 18, prompting local authorities to declare a day of mourning. Rescuers initially recovered an elderly couple from beneath the debris before the death toll rose to four on Saturday morning.

South Korea Signs Pact With EU on Satellite Network — South Korea signed an administrative agreement with the European Commission on Thursday to explore future integration with the EU’s flagship IRIS² secure satellite constellation. European Defence and Space Commissioner Andrius Kubilius and South Korean defense officials confirmed that a joint working group will evaluate system-level cooperation between Korea’s sovereign K-LEO program and IRIS², an orbital network designed as a European sovere

Switzerland Adopts Security Strategy to Counter Hybrid Threats — The Swiss government has adopted a comprehensive new security strategy featuring 10 objectives and 46 concrete measures to reinforce national defense capabilities, protect critical infrastructure, and prepare against hybrid and standoff attacks. Formulated amid Europe’s deteriorating security environment driven by Russia’s war against Ukraine, the framework emphasizes pre-arranged defense cooperation mechanisms with international p

Russia Has Attacked Ukraine’s Allies for 5 Years, Trump Says — US President Donald Trump stated on Sept. 18 that Russia has already been attacking Ukraine’s allies for “about five years,” treating Russian aggression against European partners as an established fact. His remarks follow Warsaw’s voiced concerns over cross-border threats and come amid accelerating bilateral negotiations to establish a permanent US Army base in Poland.

Putin Accuses Ukraine of Sabotaging Peace Negotiations — Russian President Vladimir Putin claimed during a Military-Industrial Commission meeting on Friday that Ukraine is actively sabotaging peace talks and taking steps to prolong the war. Despite Putin’s accusations, Ukraine has repeatedly signaled readiness for an unconditional ceasefire along the contact line and direct leader-level negotiations.

US Approves $2.68B Air Defense Equipment Sale to Ukraine — The US Department of State approved a potential $2.68 billion Foreign Military Sale to Ukraine for air defense development upgrades, equipment, and services on Sept. 18. The package includes S-300 Clone missiles, GAM-67 missiles, range-extended laser-guided rockets, ITEL 1.5 launchers, and RPS 202 counter-drone radars. The procurement will be financed through European partner contributions and previously appropriated US Foreign Military
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 18, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 18, 2026.

Moscow Expands Asset Grab Against Western Companies – Why It Could Backfire — Russia has expanded its seizure campaign against Western companies, gaining valuable assets while risking deeper capital flight and years of legal disputes.

Belarus Drone Relays Helped Russia Strike Diplomatic Train Route Near Polish Border — Belarus has reactivated drone signal relays that Kyiv says are helping Russia strike western Ukraine, including near the Polish border.

Russian Guided Bomb Tears Into Sumy Apartment Block, Killing 2, Injuring 8 — Russian guided bombs struck Sumy, killing two city employees and injuring eight civilians as rescuers searched the rubble for trapped residents.

Trump Signs Sweeping Russia Sanctions Bill Into Law — Trump signed new sanctions targeting Russia’s energy, defense and financial sectors, while giving the White House broad tariff powers over major buyers of Russian oil and gas.

‘We Won’t Let Putin Wait Us Out’: Senator Shaheen Outlines Sweeping New US Sanctions Package — Jeanne Shaheen says Congress is tightening pressure on Russia’s energy revenues and buyers such as China while pushing for more air-defense support for Ukraine.

Zelensky Urges US to Pass Lindsey Graham Sanctions Bill After Russia Strikes Sumy Apartment Block, Killing 2 — President Volodymyr Zelensky urged Washington to pass the late Senator Lindsey Graham’s bill following a Russian strike on a residential high-rise in Sumy on Friday, Sept. 18. According to RBC-Ukraine, US President Donald Trump is expected to sign the bill later today.

Ukraine Expands Business Support with Subsidized Loans, War Risk Insurance — Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi announced a new government initiative providing a 5.5% interest rate subsidy on loans up to Hr. 1 billion ($22.4 million) for key economic sectors. National Bank of Ukraine Governor Andriy Pyshny supported the initiative while addressing existing delays in the “5-7-9%” program.

Zelensky: Over 50 Carpathian Deals Worth €1B Prepared for Signing — Ukraine launched the Carpathian Eight (C8) regional initiative on Friday, with more than 50 agreements worth over €1 billion (roughly $1.1 billion) prepared for signing, according to President Volodymyr Zelensky. The investment portfolio prioritizes energy, transport, and infrastructure, while bringing together eight countries – including Moscow-leaning Serbia – to deepen regional cooperation.

Russia’s Shadow Fleet Shipments from Baltic Ports Rise 10.1%, KSE Institute Says — KSE Institute estimates that Russia exported around 5.3 mb/d of crude oil and oil products by sea in July 2026, down 10.7% m-o-m and 6.4% y-o-y. Of 268 tankers used, 150, or 56%, were shadow fleet vessels; 93% of shadow tankers were over 15 years old. Shadow fleet shipments from Baltic Sea ports rose 10.1% m-o-m and 21.2% y-o-y.

EU Allocates €100B for Ukraine in 2028-34 Budget Plan — According to European Pravda on Friday, Sept. 18, EU member states did not object to the proposal to mobilize €100 billion (about $115 billion) for Ukraine under the bloc’s next seven-year budget. The EU leaders are expected to discuss the 2028-34 financial framework during their upcoming summit held Oct. 15-16.

10 Wounded, Including 2 Rescuers, in Russian Attacks on Central Odesa — Ten people, including two rescuers, were injured in a Russian strike on a 11-story administrative building in central Odesa on Thursday, Sept. 18. Russian forces launched a second, follow-up strike on the Ukrainian as rescue crews and emergency responders while they were working at the scene.

Awarded by Putin, Eliminated by Drones: The Story of General “The Terrible” — This video breaks down the stark contrast between manufactured state propaganda, corruption, and the growing pattern of high-level Russian officer casualties.

Russia Increasingly Targeting Ukraine’s Railways, Threatening Economic, Social Security — Russia continues to systematically target Ukraine’s transport and logistics infrastructure. According to Ukrainian officials, the campaign intensified last fall, when Russia began using mesh-network technology to improve drone control and pursue moving rail targets. Belarus may have helped extend the threat to western Ukraine, including routes near the Polish border.

Russian Strikes Damage Zaporizhstal Steel Plant and Kyivstar Facility — Russian attacks on Sept. 17 damaged industrial workshops at the Zaporizhstal steel plant in Zaporizhzhia and a Kyivstar equipment facility in the Kyiv region. While one worker was injured at the steel plant, no casualties or service outages were reported by Kyivstar.

Hungary Says It Can Quit Russian Gas Within a Year — Hungary could secure its gas supply entirely from non-Russian sources by October 2027, Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said. Budapest is also negotiating with Croatia over using the Adria pipeline at full capacity to replace Russian oil, although no formal decision to end Russian imports has been announced.

Putin Transfers Russian Assets of Auchan, Nestlé to External Manager — Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a decree transferring the Russian assets of French retailer Auchan, Swiss food giant Nestlé, and logistics firms FM Logistics and Bati Logistics to AO L.E.V. Management, a Moscow-registered company with undisclosed ownership. The same decree covers Le Monlid, the former Leroy Merlin entity. Both Auchan and Nestlé scaled back Russian operations after 2022.

Russia Turns Training Missiles Into Deadly Weapons in Ukraine — Russia has begun using modified RM48U training missiles on a large scale against Ukraine. The less accurate weapons can exhaust scarce Patriot interceptors while allowing Moscow to stockpile Iskander, KN-23 and Zircon missiles for possible winter attacks.

Ukraine’s Inflation Reaches 8.1% as Fuel and Water Costs Rise — Ukraine’s annual consumer and core inflation both stood at 8.1% in August. Fuel and water tariffs drove costs higher, while the new harvest lowered food prices. The central bank expects damage to logistics infrastructure to add to inflation through the autumn.

Ukraine’s Defense Demands Victory Over Corruption at the Top — Russian missiles threaten Ukraine’s cities, but tolerated corruption in the presidential orbit risks destroying the trust and aid required to survive and must be ended.

Ukraine Opens New Border Checkpoint With Romania — The new Bila Tserkva-Sighetu Marmației checkpoint operates 24 hours a day and allows cars weighing up to 3.5 tons, with a projected capacity of up to 700 cars per day. The rest of the checkpoint remains under construction, while traffic can also pass through a neighboring checkpoint connecting Sighetu Marmației with the Ukrainian village of Solotvyno.

Ukraine Says It Hit Russian Orion Drone Control Station in Crimea — Ukraine’s General Staff reported strikes on an Orion drone control station in occupied Crimea, a drone launch site near Donetsk and two depots in the Luhansk region. The General Staff said the strikes took place on Sept. 17 and overnight into Sept. 18.

New Duma: Do the Russians Have a Choice? — Russia’s three-day parliamentary elections will elect the 450-member Duma, regional lawmakers and governors. United Russia is widely expected to win, while Yabloko was barred from participating. Critics and analysts cited in the article argue the vote offers limited competition, serves to reinforce the Kremlin’s legitimacy, and could produce an increasingly militarized parliament amid the war in Ukraine.

Russia Expands Africa Corps Despite Doubts Over Its Effectiveness, Intel Says — Ukraine’s military intelligence says Russia’s Africa Corps remains capable of carrying out security and training missions but struggles with asymmetric warfare because of rigid command structures and slow decision-making. The force has suffered setbacks, particularly in Mali, while continuing to expand abroad.

Lithuania Prepares Vilnius Evacuation Routes in Case of Military Threat — Lithuania’s evacuation plan for Vilnius identifies Poland as one of three possible directions residents could take during a military threat or major crisis. Poland’s Podlaskie region is preparing to serve as a transit corridor for evacuees from the Baltic states.

Ukraine Launches Carpathian Eight Cooperation Format — Ukraine launched the Carpathian Eight (C8), a new regional cooperation format bringing together eight European countries and EU institutions. The initiative will focus on security, energy resilience, transport links, investment and cross-border economic projects.

Deepfakes, Fake News and ‘Rigged’ Vote Claims: Russia Targets France’s 2027 Election — Russian disinformation networks are targeting potential French presidential candidates with deepfakes, fabricated reports and false health claims ahead of the 2027 election, according to Ukraine’s Center for Strategic Communications. The campaigns also target France’s electoral institutions, with Telegram and anonymous websites emerging as key channels for spreading pro-Kremlin narratives.

Russia Offering Tours of ‘Sites of Military Glory’ in Donetsk and Kursk — The Kursk regional governor Alexander Khinshtein announced an initiative to offer tourists the chance to visit sites where the Russian military and its allies conducted operations against Ukraine. This follows a plans to to develop so-called "military tourism" in the Russian-occupied part of the Donetsk region announced in late 2025.

Ukraine Drones Make Orchestrating Russia’s Elections Tougher — Voting in Sochi halted Friday amid Ukrainian drone alerts as officials ordered voters underground. One drone reportedly damaged a polling station. Broader strikes hit election sites, killed a collaborator in occupied Zaporizhzhia, and caused power outages in Kherson. Russia claimed 629 drones downed as national elections for the State Duma proceeded under threat.

Tusk, Nawrocki Clash Over Poland ‘Giving Up Territory’ in WWII Statement — A historical post by Polish President Karol Nawrocki triggered a public dispute with Prime Minister Donald Tusk after it said Poland could lose or “surrender” territory without surrendering its homeland. Nawrocki defended the wording as a reference to World War II and later warned that Russia “does not change.”

‘Waiting for Death’: Russian-Occupied Oleshky Faces Starvation as Russia Blocks Aid and Evacuation — Thousands of civilians in Russian-occupied Oleshky and nearby settlements face severe food and medicine shortages after the last confirmed delivery on May 26. UN monitors and local officials say mines and drone attacks have cut evacuation routes, while Russia has failed to confirm its readiness to proceed with a negotiated humanitarian mission despite the Red Cross’s readiness to help.

Russia’s First Duma Election Since the Full-Scale Invasion: What’s the Significance? — Russia’s first parliamentary election since the full-scale invasion will renew the legislature that approves wartime spending, conscription measures, and repressive laws. With Yabloko excluded from the national ballot, opposition figures imprisoned, and independent monitoring dismantled, the result cannot credibly measure freely expressed support for the war.

Slovakia’s Fico Pours Cold Water on Fulfilling NATO’s Article 5 Mutual Defense — The Slovak prime minister said he did not want Slovakia drawn into a war “because of some Article 5,” while criticizing what he called increasingly belligerent rhetoric in Europe. NATO’s collective-defense clause requires allies to assist an attacked member but allows each country to determine what action it considers necessary.

Russia Claims Bucha Massacre Was a Western Fabrication – But Why? — The TASS press conference was held on Sept. 17 to present a report by Maxim Grigoryev, Chairman of the so-called “International Public Tribunal on Crimes by Ukrainian Neo-Nazis,” which says it shows that the 2022 Bucha massacre was a poorly executed hoax conducted by Ukraine and Western intelligence agencies.

Russia Is Holding an ‘Election,’ Ukraine Is Defending Democracy — While Ukraine discusses restoring elections amid wartime conditions, Russia is holding a non-competitive vote domestically and unlawfully expanding it into Ukrainian-occupied areas. This is a travesty of democracy.

Trump Administration Weighs Russia Business Deals Before Ukraine War Ends – NYT — Trump’s administration is considering business deals with Russia before the war in Ukraine ends, The New York Times reported. The potential shift would mark a departure from Washington’s previous position that economic ties with Moscow should follow a peace agreement.

The Final Decision on Graham’s Sanctions Bill Rests With Trump | Stefan Korshak — The US House of Representatives is considering a new sanctions bill targeting Russia. But what would it actually mean for the Kremlin?

Russia Opens Three-Day Election as Kremlin Tests War Support — Russia has opened a three-day parliamentary election widely expected to deliver another victory for Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party. With meaningful opposition sidelined, the vote offers the Kremlin a gauge of public support for the war as Ukrainian strikes increasingly reach deep inside Russia.

Canada-Ukraine 100-Year Partnership: What Does It Mean for Both Countries? — Canada has historically been one of Ukraine’s most reliable allies, especially in this war against Russia. The new 100-year partnership framework creates much broader opportunities for both Ukraine and Canada.

Trump Says ‘Major Progress’ Being Made on Potential US Army Base in Poland — US President Donald Trump said “major progress” is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland, with the location expected to be announced soon. Two sites are under consideration, while Warsaw seeks a permanent US military presence. About 10,000 US troops currently serve in Poland, mostly on rotational deployments.

Military Airfield Repeatedly Targeted in Rostov as 50+ Drone Swarm Hits Region Again — More than 50 drones were reportedly downed over Russia’s Rostov Region overnight, with a military airfield possibly targeted again. The attack caused damage to homes, vehicles and infrastructure, according to local authorities. Ukraine has not officially confirmed responsibility for the overnight strikes.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 17, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 17, 2026.

Meloni: Putin Seeks European Escalation to Mask Ukraine Failures — Giorgia Meloni says Putin is seeking escalation with Europe to divert attention from the Ukraine battlefield and renewed her call for a unified European envoy on Kyiv.

Tusk: Intelligence Warns Russia Plans ‘Accidental’ Hybrid Strikes Against Ukraine’s Allies — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk says intelligence assessments indicate Russia may use deniable drone and missile strikes against countries supporting Ukraine.

Russia Threatens EU With Court Action as Europe Advances ‘Aggressor Pays’ Model for Ukraine — Russia is challenging EU protections around frozen sovereign assets as Europe advances an “aggressor pays” model linking Moscow’s wealth to Ukraine’s defense and reparations.

GM Defense Joins Lockheed Martin to Speed Patriot PAC-3 Missile Production — GM Defense has begun supplying Lockheed Martin with PAC-3 MSE components, delivering its first batch in just 22 days as the US moves to accelerate Patriot missile production.

Turkey Proposes Russia-Ukraine Black Sea Pact Similar to Grain Deal — Turkey has sent Russia and Ukraine a draft proposal aimed at protecting civilian shipping in the Black Sea amid a rise in attacks on commercial vessels.

Russian Drone Attack on Kyiv Injures Man, Hits Non-Residential Building — A Russian drone attack on Kyiv injured one man in the Podilskyi district, following an overnight assault that wounded 20 people across the capital.

EU Allocated €3.3B to Ukraine for Drones, Missiles — The European Union will disburse €3.3 billion (roughly $3.7 billion) to Ukraine on Friday, Sept. 18, European Commission President Ursula Von der Leyen said after speaking with President Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday. The leaders also discussed joint defense projects and Ukraine’s broader funding needs.

Warsaw Signals Readiness for US Army Base in Poland — US President Donald Trump said progress has been made toward establishing an US Army base in Poland. Polish President Karol Nawrocki confirmed the claims by responding that Warsaw is ready to strengthen defense ties and provide the “best possible location.” However, no final agreement has been announced yet.

Major General Nikoliuk Leaves Operational Command East — Major General Viktor Nikoliuk said on Thursday, Sept. 17 that he is stepping down from his post as commander of Ukraine’s Operational Command East, leaving his 5-month long tenure. Forces under his command contained Russian advances near Oleksandrivka and strengthened defenses across five eastern frontline sectors, he said.

Russia Holds Early State Duma Voting in Occupied Ukraine as Armed Troops Accompany Mobile Polling Teams — Russia has begun early voting ahead of its scheduled Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections. In occupied parts of Ukraine, mobile polling teams were deployed and accompanied by armed servicemen and police. Kyiv condemned the elections, while Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the process a “farce.”

US DFC Approves Loans for Vodafone Ukraine, Energy Giant DTEK — The US DFC is backing DTEK and Vodafone Ukraine with major infrastructure loans. The funds aim to stabilize the national energy grid using massive battery systems and upgraded critical telecom networks.

Ukraine Negotiates Second ERA Loan, Weighs Russian Collateral for 2027 Budget — Ukraine's economic bloc is negotiating a second Extraordinary Revenue Acceleration loan while exploring wider use of Russia's frozen sovereign assets as collateral, Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko and central bank governor said. The push comes as Kyiv submits a record $162 billion 2027 budget with a widening deficit and a $32.6 billion external financing gap still unresolved with partners.

3 Killed, 5 Injured in More Than 40 Russian Attacks on Dnipropetrovsk Region — Russian forces carried out more than 40 drone, artillery, and guided aerial bombs (KABs) across five districts of Dnipropetrovsk region on Thursday, Sept. 17. Three people were killed and five wounded, while private civilian property and infrastructure sustained damage.

8 Wounded in Russian FPV Drone Strike on Bus in Zaporizhzhia — A Russian first-person-view (FPV) drone struck a passenger bus near a public transport stop in Zaporizhzhia’s Kosmichnyi district on Thursday, Sept. 17, injuring eight people. The strike reflects Russia’s approach of targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, including transport. All five victims were hospitalized, with one person remaining in serious condition.

Poland's Tusk to Visit Ukraine on Friday — Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said he’s visiting Ukraine on Friday, Sept. 18, and added that his Slovak counterpart would also be there. The planned visit followed multiple Russian attacks along the Polish-Ukrainian border, with Moscow recently raising the rhetoric by threatening to level Warsaw “within two or three days” should a war break out.

NBU Raises Key Rate to 16% as War-Driven Inflation Tops Forecast — NBU raised its key policy rate by 0.5 percentage points on Thursday, citing persistent inflation and mounting medium-term price risks tied to the war. August inflation accelerated to 8.1%, driven largely by fuel and tariff costs. However, policymakers said they are ready to ease, but only if the security situation cools demand.

‘More Infantry, More Killed’: Russia’s Next Mobilization Could Backfire, Kyiv General Says — Russia still has more infantry than Ukraine but is increasingly experiencing its own shortages. Another mobilization would not radically improve Moscow’s battlefield position because modern warfare increasingly depends on drones, sensors and rapid strikes.

‘Very Massive Explosion’: Russian Drone Falls 4 km From Poland — A jet-powered drone fell or was destroyed about 4 kilometers from Poland during a Russian attack on western Ukraine, Polish officials said. Prime Minister Donald Tusk reported a “very massive explosion” near the Dorohusk border crossing, while Polish military aircraft were scrambled and air defenses prepared to intercept the drone if it approached Polish territory.

Interpol-Wanted Cybercrime Suspect Was Adviser to Russia’s ‘New People’ Leader, Report Says — A Russian cybercrime suspect wanted by Interpol and sought by Germany over his alleged role in the TrickBot and Conti operations also worked as an adviser to New People leader Vladislav Davankov, appearing on the party’s State Duma candidate list before being removed.

Ukraine Repatriates 252 Bodies From Russia — Ukraine has received the bodies of 252 people in a new repatriation operation. Russia claims the remains belong to Ukrainian citizens, including military personnel, but Ukrainian experts must still conduct examinations and formally identify them.

EXPLAINED: ‘Nuclear’ US Sanctions Bill vs. Russia – Five Things to Know — The bill would impose sweeping sanctions on Russia and foreign enablers including 100 percent tariffs on major energy buyers. Trump could sign, veto, or potentially pocket-veto the bill. If it becomes law Trump’s job will be to enforce it.

Ukraine Submits Record 2027 Budget as Finance Minister Warns of Cash Strain — Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers submitted a record $162 billion budget for 2027 to parliament, with defense spending set at 43.8% of GDP. Finance Minister Serhiy Marchenko warned lawmakers of a possible liquidity crisis before the year ends, citing a $27 billion defense ministry funding gap, a $1.6 billion tax shortfall, and a $32.6 billion financing gap still being negotiated with partners for 2027.

‘It Is a Pity’: China Could Stop the War but Leans Toward Russia, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said China is politically closer to Russia than Ukraine and has failed to use its influence over Moscow to help end the war. In an NHK interview, he also proposed a Drone Deal with Japan and warned that 30,000–50,000 North Korean troops have gained real combat and drone-warfare experience in Russia, posing a wider threat to Pacific security.

Belarus Reactivates Relays Helping Russian Drones Strike Deeper Into Ukraine, Kyiv Says — Belarus has reactivated signal relays that help Russian Shahed and Gerbera drones penetrate deeper into Ukraine, Kyiv says. Ukrainian officials linked the equipment to a Sept. 13 attack near the Yahodyn border crossing with Poland and warned that Belarus is again aiding Russia’s drone campaign.

Ukraine Suffers More Civilian Deaths in 8 Months of 2026 Than All of 2025 – UN — The UN said August saw at least 372 civilians killed and 2,349 injured in Ukraine, with the total number of casualties in the first eight months of 2026 surpassing all those of 2025. The report attributed 47 percent of civilian casualties to drone and ballistic missile strikes, with the majority occurring in cities far from the front, including Kyiv, which suffered the highest toll.

6 Russian Aircraft Hit as Ukraine Strikes Deep Inside Russia — Ukraine’s SBU hit one An-12 plane, two An-26 aircraft, and three unspecified helicopters at a Russian military airfield. A separate joint operation targeted the Yaroslavl refinery, while the president also reported unspecified “good results” in the Black Sea.

Russia Employs 25,000 North Koreans in Drone Production — Up to 25,000 North Korean citizens are working in Russia to manufacture Iranian-designed drones for the war against Ukraine, in violation of UN sanctions. This is according to a report by the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT), cited by Bloomberg and South Korea’s SBS News on Thursday, Sept. 17.

Zelensky Names Anton Kovalsky Acting Prosecutor General — President Volodymyr Zelensky appointed 42-year-old Anton Kovalsky acting prosecutor general, two days after parliament backed Ruslan Kravchenko’s dismissal. Kovalsky, previously the Khmelnytskyi regional prosecutor, inherits an office shaken by an alleged call center protection scheme and a bitter confrontation with Ukraine’s independent anti-corruption agencies that has raised concerns about the country’s reform record.

FSB Accuses Sevastopol Man of Supplying Weapons to Ukraine — The FSB Public Relations Center reported on Thursday that it had arrested a resident of Sevastopol who had organized the smuggling of weapons into the combat zone in Ukraine, on behalf of the SBU.

Russian Drone Hits Kharkiv Mall, Woman Needs Medical Aid — A Russian drone struck a shopping center in Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district on Thursday, regional authorities said. A 65-year-old employee who sheltered during the attack later became unwell and sought medical assistance. Officials reported no direct injuries from the impact, while emergency crews continued working at the scene.

Zelensky Hails ‘Powerful’ US Sanctions Bill After Overnight Russian Missile, Drone Attack — Zelensky welcomed the US House’s passage of a sweeping Russia sanctions bill after an overnight Russian attack injured civilians and damaged infrastructure in eight Ukrainian regions. The bill gives Trump expanded sanctions powers and authority to impose tariffs of up to 100%.

Ukraine Hits Russian Airfield, Major Oil Refinery in Massive Overnight Drone Attack — Ukraine’s SBU confirmed strikes on a Russian military airfield in Rostov-on-Don and the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl. The SBU said three aircraft and three helicopters were hit at the airfield, while a fire broke out at the refinery.

Associate Membership – Appreciated in Canada; a Non-Starter in Ukraine? — The EU’s proposed “associate membership” for Canada could create a new model for closer integration without full accession. But Ukraine, which has sought EU membership and stronger security guarantees, views such an arrangement as insufficient compared with full integration.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, September 16, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on September 16, 2026.

After 25 Freed in Belarus, Tsikhanouskaya Says Hundreds Still Remain Behind Bars — With the welcomed release of 25 political prisoners, Belarusian opposition leader Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya reminded the world that negotiations must continue until all those jailed for political reasons are free.

US House Passes Sweeping Russia Sanctions Bill, Sends It to Trump — The House passed a major Russia sanctions package aimed at cutting the financial networks sustaining Moscow’s war against Ukraine and increasing pressure on Putin.

Russian Strike Hits 19-Story Odesa Apartment Block, Injures 7 Including Child — A Russian strike on Odesa injured seven people, including a three-year-old child, and damaged a 19-story apartment block and nearby homes.

Russian Attack on Kyiv Injures 20, Including 2 Children, Hits Water Infrastructure — A Russian missile and drone attack injured 20 people in Kyiv, including two children, and damaged homes, offices and warehouses across the capital.

Zelensky’s Former Comedy Studio Hit in Russian Strike – It’s the Symbolism Moscow Is After — A Russian strike destroyed decades of Kvartal 95 history, turning Zelensky’s former studio into a symbol of how Moscow reaches for symbolism when it cannot defeat Ukraine on the battlefield.

Ukrainian Parliament Passes Key First-Reading Reforms for Parcel Tax and Small Business Bankruptcy — On Sept. 16, the Verkhovna Rada approved two key draft bills in their first readings to meet international commitments under IMF and EU programs. Lawmakers backed No. 16051-1 to end VAT exemptions on international parcels under €150 ($170), expected to generate Hr.10 billion ($224 million) annually.
